chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Hadeed, from Jameel ibn Darraj, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two (peace be upon them), who said:
The cursing (li'an) does not occur except by the denial of a child. And he said: When a man slanders his wife, he would curse her.
ai.seo_question: What is the condition for Li'an to take place according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the specific juristic condition that Li'an is triggered by the denial of paternity (nafi al-walad), linking the husband's accusation directly to the child's lineage. It clarifies that the ritual is not merely a response to general adultery but is specifically necessitated when the husband disputes the child's origin, a key distinction in Shia fiqh for determining the child's status. This mechanism serves as a formal legal procedure to resolve disputes over lineage without requiring additional witnesses.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Hadeed, from Jameel Bin Darraj, from Muhammad Bin Muslim, 
(It has been narrated) from one of the two (5th or the 6th Imam<sup>asws</sup>) having said: ‘The cursing does not happen except by the denial of a child’.
And he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘When the man slanders his wife, he would curse her’.
en.sarwar: 16. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Hadid from Jamil ibn Darraj from Muhammad ibn Muslim who has said the following: “One of the two Imam, (abu Ja‘far or abu ‘Abd Allah), Alayhim al-Salam, has said, ‘al-Li‘an (condemnation) does not take place without denying the child.’
He (the Imam) said, ‘When a man accuses his woman he can go through the process of al-Li‘an (condemnation) against her.’”
